title: metering-multiplexed-rate-ladder-with-customer-granularity
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Problem: Current billing attribution aggregates tokens at a per-request surface that makes per-customer rate-ladder and nested discounting both slow and error-prone. We see frequent off-by-one attribution in bursty workloads and inability to apply tiered pricing deterministically across multiple concurrent routes. This ticket builds a new multiplexed rate-ladder layer in the metering pipeline that computes per-customer, per-tier token buckets and produces an exportable claims feed used by billing jobs.

Scope: Implement end-to-end pipeline changes across ingestion -> aggregation -> claim generation -> export. This includes: a) rate-ladder evaluator component that consumes token events and tenant metadata, b) deterministic attribution algorithm to split tokens across tiers/discounts, c) an idempotent claims store with conflict resolution on duplicate ingestion, and d) a compact export format for the billing reconciler.

Constraints: Must be backward-compatible with existing billing exports for a rolling migration. Memory footprint per worker must stay under 4GB for typical tenant distribution. Processing latency for hot tenants must not exceed 250ms per batch for 95th percentile.

Why unique: Unlike the earlier reconciliation jobs which operate as batch reconciliation or ledger harmonization, this work creates a streaming-aware rate-ladder evaluator that reasons about ordered token sequences and deterministic tier attribution in real-time, enabling predictable pricing results for reserved/dedicated customers and reduced downstream correction churn.
acceptance_criteria: New rate-ladder evaluator successfully computes tiered claims for synthetic tenant workloads with >99.995% determinism compared to a canonical simulator
Stream exporter produces compact claim messages (<=1KB) and is consumed by billing-reconciler without schema changes during canary
End-to-end tests that simulate concurrent route usage and discounts show <0.1% drift versus ground truth over 24h test window
Memory usage per worker < 4GB on representative instance types
No customer-visible billing deltas during incremental rollout on 5 pilot tenants (manual verification)
design_decisions: Use event-time ordering with tenant-scoped sequence tokens to ensure deterministic splits even under out-of-order arrival
Employ a two-stage attribution: (1) fast in-memory accumulator for immediate claims, (2) durable idempotent write to claims-store (Cosmos->Postgres shim) to enable retries
Represent rate-ladders as compact protobufs with versioning to allow future feature flags without breaking export consumers
Perform migration via dual-writing: the serving ingestion will write both the legacy ledger and the new claims feed for pilot tenants until roll-forward is validated
rollout_plan: 1) Implement evaluator and local end-to-end tests in feature branch. 2) Deploy evaluator behind feature flag to staging; enable canary export to internal billing-reconciler for 2 non-prod tenants. 3) Run 72-hour soak with synthetic traffic and reconcile outputs against simulator. 4) Enable dual-write for 5 low-risk production tenants for 7 days; manually validate invoices and dashboards. 5) Gradually expand to 30% of tenants with automated drift checks; if drift <0.05% proceed to full cutover. 6) Disable legacy export once stable and update docs & runbook.
monitoring: Determinism drift metric: percent of claims differing from simulator baseline
Exporter failure rate and retry counts
Claims-store write conflicts resolved per minute
Cost estimate delta: projected monthly revenue delta for active tenants during pilot
